subject.title: Sub-agent timeout recovery creates duplicate API posts (idempotency gap)

question: Should OpenClaw add a core durable logical-action idempotency and replay contract for sub-agent side effects, and what identity boundary should it use?
rationale: The remaining gap spans core agent, gateway, tool, and external side-effect semantics; choosing the wrong boundary could either duplicate external actions or suppress legitimate repeated actions.

options.title: Design a narrow core contract
options.body: Define logical action identity, payload digest, expiry, replay response, and audit behavior first, then implement the smallest core/gateway change that protects sub-agent retries.

options.title: Limit core to exact-key dedupe
options.body: Treat the merged message-tool mitigation and existing gateway exact-key dedupe as the supported core behavior, leaving external API idempotency to workflows and plugins.

options.title: Route to ClawHub guidance
options.body: Keep core unchanged and point unattended multi-agent operators to ClawHub skills and service-specific idempotency keys.

recommendation.title: Design a narrow core contract
recommendation.body: Define logical action identity, payload digest, expiry, replay response, and audit behavior first, then implement the smallest core/gateway change that protects sub-agent retries.

likelyOwner.reason: Peter Steinberger has the strongest feature-history trail across the subagent registry and delivery-state surfaces where this contract would need approval.
